drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 56-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.88, creatinine 1.07, hemoglobin 13.9, platelets 268, sodium 141, wbc 8.7; vitals dbp 70-76, heart_rate 73-78, map 92-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 134-140, spo2 94-95, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Normal saline 1 L IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. COPD. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia; mild drop is dilutional.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.04, hemoglobin 13.6, platelets 266, sodium 140, wbc 8.3; vitals dbp 72-74, heart_rate 73-77, map 92-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 133-139, spo2 94-96, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. COPD. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia; mild drop is dilutional. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 56-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. COPD. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia; mild drop is dilutional. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
